Summary:

Sattin, Nardin, and colleagues designed and evaluated corrective microlenses that increase the useable field of view of two long (>6mm) thin (500 um diameter) GRIN lenses used in deep-tissue two-photon imaging. This paper closely follows the thread of earlier work from the same group (esp. Antonini et al, 2020; eLife), filling out the quiver of available extended-field-of-view 2P endoscopes with these longer lenses. The lenses are made by a molding process that appears practical and easy to adopt with conventional two-photon microscopes.

Simulations are used to motivate the benefits of extended field of view, demonstrating that more cells can be recorded, with less mixing of signals in extracted traces, when recorded with higher optical resolution. In vivo tests were performed in piriform cortex, which is difficult to access, especially in chronic preparations.

The design, characterization, and simulations are clear and thorough, but they do not break new ground in optical design or biological application. However, the approach shows much promise, including for applications such as miniaturized GRIN-based microscopes. Readers will largely be interested in this work for practical reasons: to apply the authors' corrected endoscopes to their own research.

Strengths:

The text is clearly written, the ex vivo analysis is thorough and well supported, and the figures are clear. The authors achieved their aims, as evidenced by the images presented, and were able to make measurements from large numbers of cells simultaneously in vivo in a difficult preparation.

The authors did a good job of addressing issues I raised in initial review, including analyses of chromaticity and the axial field of view, descriptions of manufacturing and assembly yield, explanations in the text of differences between ex vivo and in vivo imaging conditions, and basic analysis of the in vivo recordings relative to odor presentations. They have also shortened the text, reduced repetition, and better motivated their approach in the introduction.

## Review text

DOI: [10.7554/eLife.101420.4.sa2](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.101420.4.sa2)

In this manuscript, the authors present an approach to correct GRIN lens aberrations, which primarily cause a decrease in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), particularly in the lateral regions of the field-of-view (FOV), thereby limiting the usable FOV. The authors propose to mitigate these aberrations by designing and fabricating aspherical corrective lenses using ray trace simulations and two-photon lithography, respectively; the corrective lenses are then mounted on the back aperture of the GRIN lens.

This approach was previously demonstrated by the same lab for GRIN lenses shorter than 4.1 mm (Antonini et al., eLife, 2020). In the current work, the authors extend their method to a new class of GRIN lenses with lengths exceeding 6 mm, enabling access to deeper brain regions as most ventral region of the mouse brain. Specifically, they designed and characterized corrective lenses for GRIN lenses measuring 6.4 mm and 8.8 mm in length. Finally, they applied these corrected long micro-endoscopes to perform high-precision calcium signal recordings in the olfactory cortex.

Compared with alternative approaches using adaptive optics, the main strength of this method is that it does not require hardware or software modifications, nor does it limit the system's temporal resolution. The manuscript is well-written, the data are clearly presented, and the experiments convincingly demonstrate the advantages of the corrective lenses.

The implementation of these long corrected micro-endoscopes, demonstrated here for deep imaging in the mouse olfactory bulb, will also enable deep imaging in larger mammals such as rats or marmosets.

Summary:

This work presents the development, characterization and use of new thin microendoscopes (500µm diameter) whose accessible field of view has been extended by the addition of a corrective optical element glued to the entrance face. Two microendoscopes of different lengths (6.4mm and 8.8mm) have been developed, allowing imaging of neuronal activity in brain regions >4mm deep. An alternative solution to increase the field of view could be to add an adaptive optics loop to the microscope to correct the aberrations of the GRIN lens. The solution presented in this paper does not require any modification of the optical microscope and can therefore be easily accessible to any neuroscience laboratory performing optical imaging of neuronal activity.

Strengths:

(1) The paper is generally clear and well written. The scientific approach is well structured, and numerous experiments and simulations are presented to evaluate the performance of corrected microendoscopes. In particular, we can highlight several consistent and convincing pieces of evidence for the improved performance of corrected microendoscopes:

- PSFs measured with corrected microendoscopes 75µm from the centre of the FOV show a significant reduction in optical aberrations compared to PSFs measured with uncorrected microendoscopes.

- Morphological imaging of fixed brain slices shows that optical resolution is maintained over a larger field of view with corrected microendoscopes compared to uncorrected ones, allowing neuronal processes to be revealed even close to the edge of the FOV.

- Using synthetic calcium data, the authors showed that the signals obtained with the corrected microendoscopes have a significantly stronger correlation with the ground truth signals than those obtained with uncorrected microendoscopes.

(2) There is a strong need for high quality microendoscopes to image deep brain regions in vivo. The solution proposed by the authors is simple, efficient and potentially easy to disseminate within the neuroscience community.

Weaknesses:

Weaknesses that were present in the first version of the paper were carefully addressed by the authors.

results.result: Ray-trace optical simulations predicted that aspherical corrective lenses designed using iterative optimization (Strehl ratio >0.8 criterion) would increase the diffraction-limited FOV radius by 3.50× and 3.35× for 6.4 mm and 8.8 mm GRIN rods, respectively, with improved PSF regularity at off-axis positions.
results.evaluation: The simulation methodology is clearly described with appropriate optical design criteria (Maréchal criterion, Strehl ratio threshold of 0.8). The claims are internally consistent and supported by Figure 1 showing simulated PSFs and Strehl ratio distributions. The iterative optimization approach and specific lens profiles are documented in supplementary materials.

results.result: Aspherical corrective lenses were successfully fabricated using 3D two-photon lithography microprinting to create prototypes, followed by PDMS molding for rapid, cost-effective replication onto glass coverslips.
results.evaluation: The fabrication methodology is well-documented with SEM images (Figure 2A-B) confirming lens structure and a clear molding workflow (Figure 2C). The authors report ~90% yield for molding and 100% assembly success (n=27), providing quantitative validation of the manufacturing process.

results.result: Experimental characterization using subresolved fluorescent films demonstrated that corrected microendoscopes maintained more homogeneous FWHM values across extended FOV, with measured effective FOV radius increases of 2.17× (6.4 mm) and 1.53× (8.8 mm), corresponding to 4.7× and 2.3× area enlargements.
results.evaluation: The experimental measurements (Figure 3A-D, Table 1) provide quantitative validation with appropriate replicates (n=3-4 microendoscopes). The use of subresolved films (~300 nm thickness) is appropriate for PSF characterization. The measured improvements are somewhat lower than simulated predictions (2.17× vs 3.50× for 6.4 mm), which the authors acknowledge and explain through multiple factors including emission aberrations and experimental variability.

results.result: In fixed brain slices expressing jGCaMP7f, corrected microendoscopes clearly resolved neuronal somata and processes in lateral FOV portions that appeared dim, aberrated, and barely detectable with uncorrected microendoscopes.
results.evaluation: Figure 4 provides direct visual comparison showing improved cellular resolution across the FOV with corrected microendoscopes. The same tissue region was imaged with both probe types, providing an appropriate within-sample control. The qualitative improvement is evident, though quantitative metrics would strengthen the claim.

results.result: Synthetic calcium imaging data, generated using anatomical parameters from mouse olfactory cortex and jGCaMP8f biophysics, demonstrated that corrected microendoscopes enabled detection of more ROIs with high SNR (>15) and extended the maximal radial distance for high-SNR detection.
results.evaluation: The simulation framework is well-designed with biologically realistic parameters (cell size, density from Suzuki & Bekkers 2010, 2011; indicator kinetics from Zhang et al. 2023). Statistical comparisons using Mann-Whitney U tests show significant differences (Figure 5B,E,C,F, p<0.05 to p<0.001, n=13-15 simulated experiments). The ground truth comparison is a strength of this approach.

results.result: Analysis of synthetic calcium data using GLM-based purity metrics showed that corrected microendoscopes reduced artificial correlations between adjacent neurons, maintained higher purity indices across radial distances (significantly smaller slope), and improved correlation with ground truth signals, indicating reduced signal cross-contamination.
results.evaluation: The GLM analysis provides rigorous quantification of source mixing (Figure 6). Statistical tests appropriately use permutation tests for non-normal distributions (p<10^-10 for slope comparisons). The purity index methodology is sound and the results are consistent across both microendoscope lengths. The connection between improved PSF and reduced cross-contamination is logically supported.

results.result: In vivo two-photon calcium imaging in awake mice using 8.8 mm corrected microendoscopes in olfactory cortex showed constant peak SNR across FOV, no dependence of adjacent neuron pairwise correlation on radial distance (slope not significantly different from zero, p=0.089), and distance-dependent decrease in correlation for all neuron pairs.
results.evaluation: The in vivo validation (Figure 8, n=240 neurons from 6 FOVs) provides appropriate statistical analysis using linear regression and permutation tests. The finding that adjacent neuron correlation is independent of radial distance (p=0.089) supports the claim of reduced artificial correlation from improved optics. The distance-dependent decrease in all-pair correlation (p=2×10^-5) is biologically plausible and consistent with known olfactory cortex connectivity.

results.result: Experimental measurements of optical performance generally agreed with simulation predictions, though measured PSFs were larger than simulated PSFs, likely due to emission aberrations, consideration of only first-order aberrations in simulations, and experimental variability not captured in modeling.
results.evaluation: The authors appropriately acknowledge discrepancies between simulation and experiment (C89-C91) and provide plausible explanations. The simulations modeled excitation PSFs while measurements included emission, which is a valid limitation. The transparency about model limitations and experimental-theoretical agreement strengthens rather than weakens the overall conclusions.

results.result: The improvement in spatial resolution was attributed exclusively to the corrective lens, as uncorrected controls included glass coverslips that partially compensate for GRIN aberrations, suggesting that comparison to bare GRIN lenses would show even greater improvement.
results.evaluation: The experimental design appropriately includes glass coverslips in both corrected and uncorrected conditions (C93), isolating the effect of the corrective lens. The citation to Murray & Levene 2012 (C94) supports the claim that coverslips provide partial correction. The speculation about greater improvement vs. bare GRIN lenses (C95) is reasonable but appropriately framed as speculation.

results.result: The extended FOV achieved by aberration correction was characterized by a curved focal plane, meaning cells at different radial positions were at different axial positions, with peripheral cells closer to the microendoscope front end.
results.evaluation: This is a direct consequence of the optical design and is supported by the simulation data (Figure 1—figure supplement 2). The authors transparently acknowledge this characteristic, which is important for interpreting imaging results. The curved focal plane is a trade-off inherent to the correction approach.

results.result: The improved optical performance (increased high-SNR ROIs, reduced source mixing, stable purity) is essential for unbiased characterization of neuronal population codes, as artificial correlations from source mixing would bias estimates of neuron-to-neuron communication and inflate redundant over synergistic correlations.
results.evaluation: The logical argument connecting optical performance to population coding analysis is sound and supported by citations (Ecker et al. 2010, Panzeri et al. 2022). The claims about bias from artificial correlations (C102-C103) are well-reasoned. While the population coding implications are somewhat speculative, they are appropriately framed and logically follow from the demonstrated improvements in signal quality.

results.result: Long corrected microendoscopes offer advantages over alternative aberration correction methods (adaptive optics, plano-convex lenses) by providing ready-to-use correction without microscope hardware/software modifications, no temporal resolution limitations, and compatibility with portable microscopes, though previous 3D microprinting methods were limited to <4.1 mm GRIN lenses.
results.evaluation: The comparison with alternative methods is well-supported by appropriate citations (C32-C39). The claimed advantages (C114-C115) are logical consequences of the built-in correction approach. The identification of the gap in prior work (C41-C42) appropriately motivates the current study. The claims are appropriately framed as advantages rather than absolute superiority.

results.result: GRIN lenses have intrinsic optical aberrations that severely degrade imaging performance by distorting PSF, enlarging excitation volume, and reducing SNR and spatial resolution especially in lateral FOV portions, with effects particularly relevant for long (>6 mm) GRIN lenses needed for deep brain imaging.
results.evaluation: These claims about GRIN lens limitations are well-established in the literature and supported by multiple citations (Bortoletto et al. 2011, Lee & Yun 2011, Wang & Ji 2012, 2013, Antonini et al. 2020). The claims accurately represent prior knowledge and appropriately motivate the need for the current work.

results.result: The improved optical characteristics of corrected microendoscopes enhance olfactory cortex research by enabling: (1) better decoding of ensemble information, (2) exploration of individual mouse differences, (3) improved cell segmentation and motion correction in awake/behaving mice, and (4) facilitated cell tracking in chronic imaging experiments.
results.evaluation: These claims about research implications (C108-C113) are logical extensions of the demonstrated improvements and are appropriately supported by citations where relevant (Harris et al. 2016, Brondi et al. 2020, Berners-Lee et al. 2023). The claims are framed as capabilities enabled by the technology rather than as demonstrated results, which is appropriate.

results.result: The developed corrected microendoscopes (6.4 mm and 8.8 mm length, 500 μm diameter) provide a unique combination of high homogeneous optical properties, minimal invasiveness, and ready-to-use implementation that will improve 2P imaging in deep brain areas of mice and larger mammals.
results.evaluation: The specifications (C88) are clearly documented in Table 2. The claimed combination of features (C117-C118) is supported by the experimental validation. The forward-looking claim about impact on larger mammals (C119) is appropriately framed as a prediction and supported by relevant citations, though actual validation in these species would be needed.

results.result: The authors designed corrective lenses for long GRIN rods (6.4 mm and 8.8 mm) using optical simulations. Simulations predicted that corrective lenses would increase the diffraction-limited FOV radius by 3.50× and 3.35× for the two probe lengths, respectively, and improve PSF quality across the FOV.
results.evaluation: All reviewers affirm the simulation work. Reviewer 1 states 'the design, characterization, and simulations are clear and thorough,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'numerous experiments and simulations are presented to evaluate the performance.' No concerns are raised about the simulation methodology or predictions.

results.result: The authors fabricated corrective lenses using 3D microprinting based on 2P lithography to create prototypes, then replicated them using a molding procedure for efficient production.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'the lenses are made by a molding process that appears practical and easy to adopt,' indicating acceptance of the fabrication approach. Reviewer 1 also mentions that the authors 'addressed issues I raised in initial review, including...descriptions of manufacturing and assembly yield,' suggesting initial concerns were resolved.

results.result: Experimental characterization using fluorescent films showed that corrected microendoscopes collected fluorescence signal over longer distances from the FOV center with more homogeneous FWHM values. The effective FOV radius increased by 2.17× and 1.53× for the 6.4 mm and 8.8 mm probes, corresponding to FOV area enlargements of 4.7× and 2.3×.
results.evaluation: The editor states the authors 'provide convincing evidence showing that the obtained field of view is significantly increased with corrected, versus uncorrected microendoscopes.' Reviewer 3 highlights 'PSFs measured with corrected microendoscopes 75µm from the centre of the FOV show a significant reduction in optical aberrations' as convincing evidence.

results.result: Imaging of fixed brain slices demonstrated that aberration correction enabled clear resolution of neuronal somata and processes in lateral FOV portions, whereas uncorrected lenses produced dim, aberrated, and hardly detectable structures in peripheral regions.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'Morphological imaging of fixed brain slices shows that optical resolution is maintained over a larger field of view with corrected microendoscopes compared to uncorrected ones, allowing neuronal processes to be revealed even close to the edge of the FOV' as convincing evidence.

results.result: Using synthetic calcium data simulating the mouse olfactory cortex, the authors showed that corrected microendoscopes enabled detection of more ROIs with higher SNR, increased the maximal radial distance for high-SNR ROIs, reduced cross-contamination between adjacent neurons, maintained higher purity of source demixing across radial distance, and improved correlation with ground truth signals.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'simulations are used to motivate the benefits of extended field of view, demonstrating that more cells can be recorded, with less mixing of signals in extracted traces.' Reviewer 3 states 'Using synthetic calcium data, the authors showed that the signals obtained with the corrected microendoscopes have a significantly stronger correlation with the ground truth signals than those obtained with uncorrected microendoscopes' as convincing evidence.

results.result: In vivo imaging in the mouse olfactory cortex using 8.8 mm corrected microendoscopes showed that peak SNR of calcium events was constant across the FOV, pairwise correlation of adjacent neurons did not depend on radial distance, and correlation between neuron pairs decreased with their reciprocal distance, demonstrating unbiased sampling of neural population activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the authors 'were able to make measurements from large numbers of cells simultaneously in vivo in a difficult preparation' and that they 'achieved their aims, as evidenced by the images presented.' Reviewer 1 also notes the authors 'did a good job of addressing issues I raised in initial review, including...basic analysis of the in vivo recordings relative to odor presentations.'

results.result: Experimental measurements of optical performance were generally in good agreement with simulation predictions, though simulated PSF sizes tended to be smaller than experimentally measured PSFs, possibly due to differences between excitation and emission PSFs, consideration of only first-order aberrations in simulations, and experimental variability.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'did a good job of addressing issues I raised in initial review, including...explanations in the text of differences between ex vivo and in vivo imaging conditions,' suggesting initial concerns about discrepancies were adequately addressed. No reviewer challenges the comparison or the authors' explanations.

results.result: Long corrected microendoscopes (6.4 mm and 8.8 mm length, 500 µm diameter) provide improved spatial resolution enabling imaging in significantly enlarged FOVs, representing powerful new tools for population imaging with unprecedented large FOV and high spatial resolution in the most ventral regions of the mouse brain with minimal invasiveness.
results.evaluation: The editor describes this as a 'valuable study' presenting a 'potentially key method' and states the approach 'can be readily adopted by neuroscientists who wish to image neuronal activity deep in the brain.' Reviewer 2 notes 'the experiments convincingly demonstrate the advantages of the corrective lenses' and that 'the implementation of these long corrected micro-endoscopes...will also enable deep imaging in larger mammals.'

results.evaluation: The editor emphasizes 'the approach described in this paper does not require any microscope or software modifications.' Reviewer 2 states 'the main strength of this method is that it does not require hardware or software modifications, nor does it limit the system's temporal resolution.'
